beats.text: Money can't buy happiness? Sorry. It can.
For years, the story was: above seventy-five thousand dollars a year, more money stops making you happier.
Then rival researchers teamed up, using an app that asked people how they felt at random moments.
For most people, happiness kept rising with income. Way past seventy-five thousand.
Only the unhappiest group leveled off, at around a hundred thousand.
So money does help. But if you're deeply unhappy, more of it won't fix everything.

sources: Killingsworth, Kahneman & Mellers (2023). Income and emotional well-being: A conflict resolved. PNAS 120(10). Adversarial collaboration; experience sampling (Track Your Happiness); happiness rises with income on average; least happy group rises until ~$100k then plateaus; earlier plateau at $75k (Kahneman & Deaton 2010) reflected the unhappy. Via ScienceDaily.
